## 3. Findings

### F-01 [P1|evidence-integrity/D-58|needs-user:false]

- **section/artifact:** §4.3.3 CONFORMING FUSION paragraph ("The
  two-quantity wording above and the fused single pass produce IDENTICAL
  observables (state at end of span, opening line M, per-record break
  count) — outcome-identity WITH THE NORMATIVE (N, M) asserted live over
  the six S-10/T-C7 corpora by appendix/66-rev14-binding-timing.py
  Part B"); same claim mirrored in the D-58 register row ("the
  table-latch shapes agree with each other AND with the normative (N, M)
  over the six S-10/T-C7 corpora") and the header probes row ("table-latch
  (every FIELD_START→QUOTED) vs first-latch … over the six S-10/T-C7
  corpora, asserting the NORMATIVE N/M").
- **claim:** the two-quantity and fused forms are outcome-identical
  (including the opening-line M), and this identity is "asserted live" by
  appendix/66 Part B.
- **evidence (live + mechanical, this cycle):** 66 Part B's identity
  check is vacuous — it never compares the two shapes:
  1. Mechanical (72b T1/T2, quoting 66 lines 377-378): the check
     "two-quantity == fused (table latch, full outcome)" is computed as
     `tq = outcome(corpus, "table")` followed by
     `fu = outcome(corpus, "table")` — the SAME function
     (`scan_span` with `latch="table"`) called twice on the same corpus.
     `tq == fu` compares one shape with itself; it cannot fail while
     Python's `==` is deterministic. No fused-shape code (no
     `count_line_breaks`-decoupled pass with a table latch) exists in
     Part B at all — the only two-quantity variant present
     (`scan_span_tq_shape`) uses the legacy FIRST-quote latch and is
     used solely to reproduce B3's blind spot.
  2. Live (72b I1, 13-corpus battery — the comparison 66 should have
     run): a REAL two-quantity build (FSM pass with the table latch +
     separate `count_line_breaks` pass) vs a REAL fused build (one pass,
     same latch) — per-record outcome identity HOLDS on all 13 corpora
     (the six S-10/T-C7 members plus 7 discriminators). The underlying
     spec claim is TRUE; the cited evidence does not execute it.
  3. The vacuity is inherited, not latent: at v13 the same identity
     claim leaned on appendix/51 B3, whose two shapes shared a wrong
     latch — adv-c13 F-02 (P2) found the evidence void and demanded a
     probe that "latches at EVERY FIELD_START→QUOTED transition …
     asserts two-quantity == fused == the normative". v14's replacement
     asserts the normative M (genuinely — the table-latch-vs-first-latch
     and N/M assertions are real checks) but silently dropped the
     shape-vs-shape half, so the specific sentence "the table-latch
     shapes agree with each other AND with the normative" (D-58 register
     row) is half-unevidenced: the "agree with each other" clause has no
     executing check.
- **minimal counterexample:** open appendix/66 lines 376-381: `tq =
  outcome(corpus, "table")`; `fu = outcome(corpus, "table")`;
  `check(… "two-quantity == fused …", tq == fu)`. Mutate the fused
  shape's semantics arbitrarily — e.g. make a hypothetical fused
  implementation advance `rel` twice per CRLF — and 66 Part B stays
  27/27 PASS, because no fused implementation participates in the
  check. Conversely, my 72b I1 runs the real comparison and passes,
  proving the fix is one battery away, not a redesign.
- **impact:** the verification plan cannot prove the claimed property
  (P1 per board policy: "the verification plan cannot prove a claimed
  property"). This is the second consecutive cycle where the D-58
  identity sentence's evidence is void (v13: shared wrong latch; v14:
  self-comparison), and D-58's latitude text says either form is
  conforming precisely because they are outcome-identical — the load-
  bearing justification of the latitude has still never been executed
  as a test.
- **required disposition:** add the missing shape-vs-shape battery to
  the living evidence: a real two-quantity (table-latch FSM pass +
  separate break pass) vs real fused (one pass) per-record outcome
  comparison over the S-10/T-C7 corpus family (72b I1 is exactly this
  and passes 13/13 — the designer may re-aim/copy it per the board's
  probe-re-aim convention, or extend 66 Part B's `fu` call to a genuine
  fused-shape function). No spec text change needed — the claim is
  true; only the evidence must exist.
- **decision owner:** spec-designer.
- **verification required:** the re-aimed/extended identity battery run
  green on the next revision; 70-class fold pins extended with a needle
  on the new battery's name.
